name: shipyard-delivery
title: Coding sessions: adding snippets or a reminder to the prompt
command: eval/skill_eval.py --bank BANK run --set all --only HELD_OUT --ask plain --cond I,R && eval/skill_eval.py grade RUNS

conditions.corpus: the shipyard corpus; the same 30 held-out questions, in both wordings
conditions.arms: the skill plus snippets from past sessions added to the prompt when its rare words match strongly; and the skill plus a one-line reminder when the prompt refers to earlier work. Neither arm has the session-start note.
conditions.grading: Claude Opus, blind, in one shuffled pass with the other arms

summary: Two ways of helping without waiting for the agent to search: put matching snippets in front of it, or remind it to search. Both are hooks that ctx has and does not install by default.
baseline: ctx as installed, with the skill and the session-start note (24.0 and 24.5 of 30)
bar: ships only if better than ctx as installed on a paired sign test at p below 0.05, with no more wrong answers (set before the run)
meaning: Neither helps, and both arms scored below ctx as installed, significantly so on paraphrased questions. The reason is that they almost never act: snippets were added for 4 and 3 of 30 questions and the reminder for 1 and 0, so these arms are in effect the skill alone. On the few questions where snippets were added, the answers were right. The session-start note remains the one thing shown to make agents search, and both hooks stay off by default.

metrics.label: Snippets added to the prompt
metrics.note: own terms and paraphrased; added for 4 and 3 questions
